Showing 1,000 of 43,266: 500 graded endpoints plus 500 with payment-term problems. Every endpoint is in scores.json. Scores cover the last 7 days; an endpoint needs 3 checks before it gets a grade. Big hosts are sampled, so most of their listings stay ungraded. Red chips are problems an agent would regret paying into; amber chips are warnings; grey chips are information only. Price shown only for dollar-denominated listings. Click a column header to sort.

How this works

Every listing in Coinbase's public x402 Bazaar catalog and in the MPP (Machine Payments Protocol) service directory is checked on a rotating schedule, about twice a day for most services. Each check asks for the resource without paying and records whether the server answered, how fast, and whether the payment terms it quotes match the listing: the same network, a wallet the listing (or the same service) names, and a price within 2× of what's listed. No wallet is involved and nothing is ever paid.

Scores weigh uptime (50%), speed (15%), whether the payment terms match the listing (20%), and paying customers in the last 30 days (15%, from the catalog; the MPP directory doesn't publish usage, so for MPP listings that part is left out rather than counted as zero). Grades need at least 3 checks in the last 7 days. Hosts with thousands of listings are sampled, so most of their listings stay ungraded. Paid-call counts and payer counts are Coinbase's own figures from the catalog.

What doesn't count against anyone: fresh payment addresses per request, paying into another wallet the same service lists, prices that vary by request (up to 2×), asking for input before quoting a price, route-pattern listings like /price/:address, rate limits, and TLS problems on our side.

Run an endpoint? Prove your payout address is yours, free: publish it on your site or DNS and sign it with the wallet. Verified endpoints get a green mark, and if anything ever asks to be paid somewhere else, the board flags it. Verify your payout address.

Is this your endpoint? If something here is wrong, or you want an alert the moment your endpoint breaks or drifts from its listing, get in touch. Corrections are welcome and fixed fast.
